Untranslatables inside language models

Main model: meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (bf16).

Summary

Draft, generated from the numbers; to be rewritten by a person.
Inside meta-llama/Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct (bf16), the part of a word English cannot rebuild separates untranslatables from ordinary words with AUROC 0.72, against 0.63 for word frequency alone. Translating between two non-English languages, up to 94% of the model's working answer is English midway through. Distinctions English lacks are mistranslated -1% more often than ones it keeps. These are first-pass numbers; read the caveats below before quoting any of them.

Figures

Figure 1

How to read this: Each bar is one word rebuilt from the English words the model finds closest inside its 'concept space'. Coloured blocks are the English ingredients, widest = most important. Solid blocks appear in nearly every context the word was read in; striped blocks only in some. Grey is what is left over: the part of the word that English could not rebuild.

Figure 2

How to read this: As in the first figure, for every untranslatable: coloured blocks are English ingredients (solid = in nearly every context, striped = only in some); grey is what English could not rebuild.

Figure 3

How to read this: Each line follows a typical word of one kind as more English words are added. Higher means more of the word has been rebuilt. The grey band is what random words of the same language reach; above it means better than chance.

Figure 4

How to read this: A flattened sketch of a small part of the model's concept space (a 2-D projection of many dimensions, so distances are only roughly right). The star is the word; labelled dots are its English ingredients; grey dots are other nearby English words.

Figure 5

How to read this: Each bar is one word; taller means more of it could not be rebuilt from English. Bars are grouped by kind of word. Striped bars are words the model did not seem to know, so they should be read with caution. The grey band is what random words reach.

Figure 6

How to read this: For each word we copy the model's inner representation of it into a prompt asking for an English word, and let it answer 50 times. Bars show how often each English answer came out. The recipe's top ingredients are listed for comparison.

Figure 7

How to read this: Each row is one untranslatable; each dot is one language it was rebuilt from (en = English, es = Spanish, ...). Further right means more is left over. A word can be hard to carry into one language and easy into another.

Figure 8

How to read this: We ask each model to translate single words between two non-English languages and peek at its working answer layer by layer. Higher means the in-between answer is more English. Aya, built to be less English-centred, is highlighted in blue.

Figure 9

How to read this: For each language and model: how much of that language's word cloud is captured by English's 50 main directions (black), and how much of English's cloud by that language's (grey). A black dot to the right of the grey one means the space is built more around English.

Figure 10

How to read this: Translating between two languages that both make a distinction English does not (savoir/connaître, ser/estar; blue) versus distinctions English also makes (look/see; grey). Taller bars mean more wrong choices.

Figure 11

How to read this: We nudge the model's inner state toward English (right) or away from it (left). Left: wrong choices on distinctions English lacks. Right: how much of the untranslatables is left over. Grey columns mark pushes strong enough to make the model's output degrade, which should not be trusted.

What this does and doesn't show

  • Everything is inside these models: it says how a model represents a word, not what the word means.
  • Frequency, token count and familiarity can each fake 'untranslatability'. The baseline comparison shows whether the leftover beats frequency and token count alone; where it does not, the result is not evidence about meaning.
  • The two-dimensional pictures are flattened sketches of spaces with thousands of dimensions.
  • Ignorance and multiplicity are separate diagnostics, not two halves of one total.
  • Word lists, contexts, glosses and distinction sentences were drafted by Claude and need checking (appendix).
  • Romanesco items have few contexts and placeholder glosses until Belli's footnotes are added.

Technical appendix

Methods and sources

  • Concept-space recipes: non-negative sparse decomposition over another language's vocabulary: [1601.03764], [2610.08303]
  • Language identity removed by centring, no Procrustes alignment: [2004.05160], [2605.24310]
  • Chance baselines by permutation: [2602.14486]
  • Nearest-neighbour (CSLS) gap baseline: [2605.24310]
  • Patching readout: [2411.08745]
  • Latent language by logit lens: [2402.10588], [2303.08112]
  • Steering toward/away from English: [2505.13141], [2502.15603]
  • Distinction collapse ('language spilling'): [2601.12549]
  • Meaning clustering and semantic entropy; kernel language entropy: [2302.09664], [2405.20003]
  • One factor at a time; diagnostics not an additive partition: [2603.24967], [2209.03302]
  • Clarification ensembling: [2311.08718]
  • Other ignorance signals: cross-model, small vs large, iterative prompting: [2604.17112], [2402.03563], [2406.02543]
  • Linear probes for ambiguity / unfamiliarity: [2506.01205]

Concept layer: 11; centring: templates: per-template pool centroid; natural/frame: mean of all targets' natural+frame contexts in that language; rom uses Italian centroids. Tuned lens not used: no pretrained lens exists for these checkpoints.

Word list, contexts and glosses (drafted by Claude; to be checked)

de:Sehnsucht — untranslatable

an intense, often bittersweet yearning for something distant, lost or unattainable

Gloss: Sehnsucht: inniges, oft schmerzliches Verlangen nach jemandem oder etwas, das fern oder unerreichbar ist. Beispiel: „Die Sehnsucht nach dem Meer ließ ihn nicht los.“

  1. Nach drei Monaten im Ausland packte sie die [[Sehnsucht]] nach ihrer Familie.
  2. In den Gedichten der Romantik ist die [[Sehnsucht]] nach dem Unendlichen allgegenwärtig.
  3. Er schaute dem Zug mit [[Sehnsucht]] hinterher.
  4. Diese [[Sehnsucht]] nach etwas, das ich nicht benennen kann, kommt jeden Herbst wieder.
  5. Die [[Sehnsucht]] nach Ruhe trieb ihn aufs Land.

Senses: longing for a person or place — Hier ist „Sehnsucht“ das starke Verlangen nach einem Menschen oder Ort, der fern ist.; yearning for the unattainable or infinite (Romantic) — Hier ist „Sehnsucht“ ein unbestimmtes Verlangen nach etwas Unerreichbarem, Fernem oder Unendlichem.

de:Heimat — untranslatable

home(land) as a place of belonging, identity and emotional attachment, not just residence

Gloss: Heimat: Ort, Gegend oder Land, wo man aufgewachsen ist oder sich zugehörig und geborgen fühlt. Beispiel: „Nach vielen Jahren im Ausland kehrte sie in ihre Heimat zurück.“

  1. Nach dem Krieg verloren viele Menschen ihre [[Heimat]].
  2. Für mich ist Musik eine Art [[Heimat]].
  3. Er spricht noch immer den Dialekt seiner [[Heimat]].
  4. Berlin ist längst ihre zweite [[Heimat]] geworden.
  5. Der Film erzählt von [[Heimat]], Abschied und Rückkehr.

Senses: homeland, place of origin — Hier ist „Heimat“ der Ort oder das Land, aus dem man stammt.; sense of belonging and identity — Hier ist „Heimat“ das Gefühl, irgendwo dazuzugehören und geborgen zu sein, unabhängig vom Ort.

de:Fernweh — untranslatable

an ache to be far away, a longing for distant places one has not been to (opposite of homesickness)

Gloss: Fernweh: Sehnsucht nach fernen Ländern und danach, zu reisen; Gegenteil von Heimweh. Beispiel: „Beim Anblick der Flugzeuge bekam er Fernweh.“

  1. Im grauen November packt mich jedes Jahr das [[Fernweh]].
  2. Die Reisekataloge verstärkten nur ihr [[Fernweh]].
  3. Er litt nicht an Heimweh, sondern an [[Fernweh]].
  4. Das [[Fernweh]] trieb sie nach dem Abitur nach Südamerika.

de:Gemütlichkeit — untranslatable

Gloss: Gemütlichkeit: Zustand von Behaglichkeit, Wärme und entspannter Geselligkeit. Beispiel: „Kerzen und ein Kachelofen sorgten für Gemütlichkeit.“

Senses: physical cosiness of a place — Hier ist „Gemütlichkeit“ die warme, behagliche Atmosphäre eines Ortes.; relaxed sociability, good company — Hier ist „Gemütlichkeit“ das entspannte, gesellige Beisammensein ohne Eile.

fr:dépaysement — untranslatable

Gloss: Dépaysement : sentiment d'être hors de son cadre habituel, qui peut être agréable (changement de décor) ou déstabilisant (perte de repères). Exemple : « Pour le dépaysement, rien ne vaut un voyage en Islande. »

  2. Les premiers mois à Paris, il a souffert d'un profond [[dépaysement]].
  3. Ce petit village offre un [[dépaysement]] total à deux heures de la ville.
  4. Le [[dépaysement]] de l'exil se lit dans ses poèmes.
  5. Les touristes viennent chercher le [[dépaysement]] et trouvent des chaînes de magasins.

Senses: unsettling disorientation, culture shock — Ici, « dépaysement » désigne le malaise de celui qui ne retrouve plus ses repères.; refreshing change of scene — Ici, « dépaysement » désigne le plaisir d'un changement complet de décor et d'habitudes.

  2. Baudelaire passait des heures à [[flâner]] dans les passages couverts.
  3. Arrête de [[flâner]] et viens m'aider !
  4. Nous avons passé l'après-midi à [[flâner]] dans les ruelles du Marais.
  5. Il n'y a pas de meilleure façon de découvrir une ville que de [[flâner]].

Senses: to stroll idly for pleasure — Ici, « flâner » veut dire se promener sans but, pour le plaisir.; to dawdle, waste time — Ici, « flâner » veut dire traîner, perdre son temps au lieu de travailler.

fr:retrouvailles — untranslatable

  1. Les [[retrouvailles]] à l'aéroport furent pleines de larmes.
  2. Après dix ans, leurs [[retrouvailles]] furent un peu maladroites.
  3. Le groupe prépare ses [[retrouvailles]] sur scène pour l'été prochain.
  4. On a fêté nos [[retrouvailles]] autour d'un bon dîner.
  5. Ces [[retrouvailles]] avec la mer m'ont fait un bien fou.

Senses: the emotional act of reunion — Ici, « retrouvailles » désigne la joie de se revoir après une longue séparation.; a reunion event or gathering — Ici, « retrouvailles » désigne une rencontre organisée entre personnes qui ne s'étaient pas vues depuis longtemps.

Gloss: Esprit de l'escalier : le fait de trouver la bonne réponse ou la remarque spirituelle seulement après coup, quand l'occasion est passée (expression venue de Diderot). Exemple : « J'ai eu l'esprit de l'escalier : la réplique parfaite m'est venue dans le métro. »

  1. J'ai eu l'[[esprit de l'escalier]] : la réplique parfaite m'est venue dans le métro.
  2. Diderot a donné son nom à l'[[esprit de l'escalier]].
  3. Souffrant d'[[esprit de l'escalier]], il rejouait toutes ses disputes la nuit.
  4. C'est l'[[esprit de l'escalier]] qui fait les meilleurs romanciers.

  3. Il y a du calcaire au fond de la [[bouilloire]].

Senses: kettle — Ici, « bouilloire » désigne l'appareil qui sert à faire bouillir de l'eau.

fr:tricoter — ordinary

  3. Il faut trois semaines pour [[tricoter]] un pull.

fr:temps — polysemous

(1) time; (2) weather; (3) tense (grammar)

Gloss: Temps : (1) durée mesurable, écoulement des heures et des jours ; (2) état de l'atmosphère à un moment donné. Exemple : « Je n'ai pas le temps » ; « Quel temps fait-il ? »

  1. Je n'ai pas le [[temps]] de lire.
  2. Quel [[temps]] fait-il à Marseille ?
  3. Le [[temps]] passe trop vite.
  4. Avec ce [[temps]], on reste à la maison.
  5. Le [[temps]] devrait s'améliorer demain.

fr:avocat — polysemous

(1) lawyer; (2) avocado

Gloss: Avocat : (1) personne dont le métier est de conseiller et de défendre des clients en justice ; (2) fruit tropical à la chair verte et onctueuse, avec un gros noyau. Exemple : « Il a pris un avocat » ; « une salade d'avocat ».

  1. Son [[avocat]] a demandé un report du procès.
  2. Coupe l'[[avocat]] en deux et retire le noyau.
  3. Elle est [[avocat]] dans un grand cabinet parisien.
  4. Cet [[avocat]] n'est pas encore mûr.

fr:ennui — loanword

Gloss:

  3. L'[[ennui]] du dimanche après-midi est légendaire.
  4. Baudelaire fait de l'[[ennui]] un thème central.

Senses: boredom — ; a problem, trouble (often plural) —

fr:déjà vu — loanword

the feeling of having already experienced the present situation

Gloss:

  2. Ce débat politique donne un sentiment de [[déjà vu]].
  3. Le [[déjà vu]] reste mal expliqué par la science.
  4. Encore un remake : quelle impression de [[déjà vu]] !
  5. Elle a ressenti un étrange [[déjà vu]] dans cette rue.

Senses: feeling of having lived this before —

it:sprezzatura — untranslatable

studied nonchalance; making difficult things look effortless (Castiglione)

Gloss: Sprezzatura: disinvoltura elegante che nasconde lo sforzo e l'artificio, termine reso celebre da Castiglione nel "Cortegiano". Esempio: "Suonava il pianoforte con una sprezzatura che incantava tutti."

  1. Castiglione raccomanda al cortigiano una certa [[sprezzatura]] in ogni cosa.
  2. Portava la giacca sbottonata con calcolata [[sprezzatura]].
  3. Risolse il problema con una [[sprezzatura]] che ci lasciò senza parole.
  4. La moda maschile italiana ha fatto della [[sprezzatura]] un marchio.
  5. Dietro quella [[sprezzatura]] c'erano anni di esercizio.

Senses: effortless grace that hides effort — Qui "sprezzatura" è la grazia disinvolta di chi fa sembrare facile una cosa difficile.; affected nonchalance, studied carelessness (style) — Qui "sprezzatura" è una trascuratezza studiata nell'abbigliamento o nei modi, fatta apposta per sembrare naturale.

it:magari — untranslatable

(interj.) if only!; (adv.) maybe, perhaps; even

Gloss: Magari: (1) esclamazione che esprime un desiderio; (2) avverbio che indica una possibilità; (3) avverbio con valore di "perfino, addirittura". Esempio: "Vinceremo?" "Magari!"; "Magari domani piove."

  1. "Hai vinto alla lotteria?" "[[Magari]]!"
  2. [[Magari]] domani piove e non possiamo andare al mare.
  3. Sarebbe capace di uscire [[magari]] anche con la febbre.
  4. Passa a trovarci, [[magari]] sabato.
  5. [[Magari]] fossi ancora giovane!

Senses: if only! (wish) — Qui "magari" esprime un desiderio forte, come per dire che si vorrebbe tanto che fosse vero.; maybe, perhaps — Qui "magari" indica una possibilità: forse, può darsi.; even, possibly (concessive) — Qui "magari" significa "perfino, addirittura", in senso ipotetico.

it:menefreghismo — untranslatable

Gloss: Menefreghismo: atteggiamento di chi ostenta indifferenza verso doveri, regole o conseguenze ("me ne frego"). Esempio: "Il menefreghismo di certi automobilisti è pericoloso."

  1. Il [[menefreghismo]] di certi automobilisti mette tutti in pericolo.
  2. Lo accusano di [[menefreghismo]] verso i problemi della città.
  3. Il [[menefreghismo]] fu esaltato dalla propaganda del Ventennio.
  4. Quel [[menefreghismo]] è solo una maschera per la sua timidezza.
  5. In ufficio regna un [[menefreghismo]] generale.

Senses: personal indifference, not caring — Qui "menefreghismo" è l'atteggiamento di chi se ne infischia delle regole e degli altri.; the Fascist-era motto 'me ne frego' as attitude — Qui "menefreghismo" indica il motto e l'atteggiamento sprezzante esaltato dal fascismo.

it:abbiocco — untranslatable

Gloss: Abbiocco: (regionale, colloquiale) improvvisa sonnolenza, specialmente dopo un pasto abbondante. Esempio: "Dopo la pasta al forno mi è venuto l'abbiocco."

  1. Dopo il pranzo della domenica arriva puntuale l'[[abbiocco]].
  2. Ho avuto un [[abbiocco]] davanti alla televisione.
  3. Per combattere l'[[abbiocco]] bevo un caffè.
  4. Alle tre del pomeriggio in ufficio è [[abbiocco]] generale.
  5. L'[[abbiocco]] mi ha preso proprio durante la riunione.

Senses: post-meal drowsiness — Qui "abbiocco" è la sonnolenza che viene dopo aver mangiato molto.

it:annaffiatoio — ordinary

  3. Il bambino gioca con un [[annaffiatoio]] di plastica.

Senses: watering can — Qui "annaffiatoio" è il recipiente per bagnare le piante.

it:domani — ordinary

  1. Passami il [[mestolo]] per il brodo.
  2. Mescola il sugo con il [[mestolo]] di legno.
  3. Il [[mestolo]] è caduto nella pentola.

  1. Non ho [[tempo]] per leggere il giornale.
  2. Con questo [[tempo]] è meglio restare a casa.

  1. Questa [[pesca]] è dolcissima.
  2. Mio padre va a [[pesca]] ogni domenica.

Gloss: Saudade: sentimento de falta e desejo de alguém ou de algo ausente, misturado com a lembrança do que se viveu. Exemplo: "Quando emigrou, levou consigo a saudade da aldeia."

  1. Desde que ela partiu para Lisboa, a [[saudade]] não me deixa dormir.
  2. O fado canta a [[saudade]] de quem ficou no cais a ver o barco partir.
  3. Tenho [[saudade]] dos verões na casa da minha avó.
  4. Há uma [[saudade]] estranha de coisas que nunca aconteceram.
  5. Mata a [[saudade]] e telefona à tua mãe.

Senses: longing for an absent person or place — Aqui, "saudade" é a falta que se sente de uma pessoa ou de um lugar que está longe.; nostalgia for a past that is gone — Aqui, "saudade" é a lembrança melancólica de um tempo passado que não volta.; wistful yearning for what never was — Aqui, "saudade" é o desejo vago de algo que talvez nunca tenha existido.

pt:cafuné — untranslatable

Gloss: Cafuné: carícia feita passando suavemente os dedos pelo cabelo ou couro cabeludo de alguém. Exemplo: "A mãe fazia cafuné no filho até ele adormecer."

  4. O gato fecha os olhos quando recebe [[cafuné]] atrás das orelhas.
  5. Adormeci no sofá com o [[cafuné]] da minha namorada.

Senses: the act of stroking someone's hair affectionately — Aqui, "cafuné" é o gesto de passar os dedos devagar pelo cabelo de alguém, com carinho.

pt:jeitinho — untranslatable

Gloss: Jeitinho: maneira hábil e informal de resolver uma situação difícil, muitas vezes contornando regras com simpatia ou conhecimentos. Exemplo: "Não havia mesa livre, mas ele deu um jeitinho e conseguimos jantar."

  1. O prazo já tinha acabado, mas o funcionário deu um [[jeitinho]] e aceitou o meu pedido.
  2. Com um [[jeitinho]] a mala acabou por fechar.
  3. Há quem diga que o [[jeitinho]] brasileiro é uma forma de sobrevivência.
  4. Ele conseguiu o emprego à base de [[jeitinho]], não de mérito.
  5. Dá um [[jeitinho]] e arranja-me dois bilhetes para o concerto.

Senses: a resourceful workaround — Aqui, "jeitinho" é uma solução engenhosa e improvisada para um problema prático.; bending rules through favours or charm — Aqui, "jeitinho" é contornar uma regra com simpatia, favores ou conhecimentos pessoais.

pt:colher — ordinary

  1. Passa-me a [[colher]], que a sopa está a arrefecer.
  2. Mexi o café com a [[colher]] e queimei os dedos.
  3. A criança deixou cair a [[colher]] no chão.
  4. Junta uma [[colher]] de açúcar à massa.
  5. Esta [[colher]] de prata era da minha bisavó.

Senses: spoon — Aqui, "colher" é o utensílio de mesa usado para comer sopa.

pt:espremedor — ordinary

Gloss: Espremedor: utensílio de cozinha usado para extrair o sumo de frutas, sobretudo citrinos. Exemplo: "Espremeu três laranjas no espremedor."

  3. Comprei um [[espremedor]] de vidro na feira.
  4. Com este [[espremedor]] faço sumo de laranja todas as manhãs.
  5. O [[espremedor]] está na gaveta de baixo.

Senses: juicer — Aqui, "espremedor" é o utensílio de cozinha para tirar o sumo das laranjas.

pt:tijolo — ordinary

brick

pt:tristeza — emotion_plain

sadness

  2. Falou da derrota sem [[tristeza]] nenhuma.
  3. Havia [[tristeza]] nos olhos da menina.
  4. A música encheu a sala de [[tristeza]].

nostalgia

pt:manga — polysemous

(1) sleeve; (2) mango

rom:schertri — dialect_known_gloss

skeletons (cf. Italian scheletri)

broody hen (a hen sitting on eggs, with her chicks)

Gloss: PLACEHOLDER (replace with Belli's footnote): "bbiocca" è la chioccia, la gallina che cova e poi raccoglie intorno a sé i pulcini. Esempio: "I pulcini corrono sotto la bbiocca."

  1. come purcini attorno de la [[bbiocca]].

Senses: broody hen — Qui "bbiocca" vuol dire la chioccia, la gallina che cova le uova e guida i pulcini.

  1. come [[purcini]] attorno de la bbiocca.

rom:bbona sera — dialect_untranslatable

rom:a ppecorone — dialect_untranslatable

on all fours, on hands and knees (from pecora, sheep)

  1. de schertri da la terra [[a ppecorone]],

Senses: on all fours — Qui "a ppecorone" vuol dire carponi, camminando sulle mani e sulle ginocchia.; like sheep, in a flock (etymological) — Qui "a ppecorone" fa pensare alle pecore, come un gregge che avanza a testa bassa.

rom:ffora a cchi ttoca — dialect_untranslatable

Gloss: PLACEHOLDER (replace with Belli's footnote): "fora a chi tocca" vuol dire "fuori chi è di turno", il grido con cui si chiama qualcuno a uscire o a presentarsi. Esempio: "Il sergente gridò: fora a chi tocca!"

fr-es_savoir-connaitre (english_lacks)
  1. Je sais qu'il viendra demain. — I know he will come tomorrow. → saber
